analyzed_vuln.description: xmlParseNCNameComplex computes a start pointer as CUR_PTR-BASE_PTR and later calls xmlDictLookupHashed(dict, BASE_PTR + startPosition, len) without ensuring the name bytes are NUL-terminated or that maxLen is bounded by available input. xmlDictLookupHashed/xmlDictLookupInternal forwards this to xmlDictHashName, which scans until either maxLen or a '\0'. Because parser input buffers can end without a terminator at that exact boundary, xmlDictHashName performs a 1-byte read past the end (ASan shows read of global empty-string literal +1), causing global-buffer-overflow.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the xml fuzz harness, a crafted document beginning with whitespace and malformed tag/name bytes drives xmlParseStartTag2 -> xmlParseQNameHashed -> xmlParseNCNameComplex with a non-terminated slice at the input boundary. The parser passes pointer+length from the current input buffer into dictionary lookup; dictionary hashing then reads one byte beyond that slice while probing for '\0'. Trigger requires reaching start-tag name parsing with input arranged so the NCName slice ends exactly at a non-owned boundary (as in provided PoC).
